text:
diego.mendez: Hey team — I just noticed two deposits for payroll today: one in USD from Redwood and a separate MXN deposit from a local payroll account. I got net pay twice and there9s a Mexican ISR deduction on the MXN paystub. I9m still on US payroll only. Can someone stop this? cc @lina.payroll

lina.payroll: Yikes. Thanks for flagging. Quick ask: can you DM me the two bank tx references and upload both paystubs to the HR portal? We9ll pause further action until we confirm amounts. :eyes:

carlos.tax: This might be a PEO/vendor duplicate run. Important to act fast because ISR withholdings in Mexico are typically remitted quickly. We need to: 1) identify whether the MX payroll was run by our local PEO, 2) request reversal if possible, and 3) confirm if Mexican payroll reported the wages (CFDI) which would trigger employer taxes and social contributions.

isabel.legal: Also confirm employment status: were you ever onboarded as a local MX employee or EOR? I know the hire record said US payroll but repeating errors happen during transfers. If vendor issued CFDI, it creates local reporting obligations.

lina.payroll: Diego, found your HR record: country=Mexico (remote), employment_type=US-employee, payroll_vendor=GlobalPayrollInc (US pay) but also shows a stale EOR flag that apparently triggered a local run. Looks like vendor mapping mismatch. I've paused recurring runs with vendor.

lina.payroll: Action checklist for Diego (please paste back):
```
- attach USD paystub and MXN paystub to portal
- confirm which bank account received which deposit
- any taxes withheld in MXN paystub? (ISR/IMSS/INFONAVIT)
- do you want us to reverse the MX net pay or keep and gross-up later?
```

diego.mendez: Uploaded both paystubs and bank refs. MXN paystub shows ISR withheld MXN 8,400 and IMSS employer/employee contributions listed. Net MXN deposit = MXN 28,600. USD deposit = $1,650 (matches expected). I prefer reversal of MX net pay if possible.

carlos.tax: If MX payroll already issued CFDI with tax withholding, reversal is more complex. We should ask PEO to: 1) reverse the net payment (bank recall), 2) cancel CFDI and file complement of cancellation with SAT, and 3) refund any employer-side contributions if remitted. If CFDI can't be canceled quickly, we may need to gross-up or reimburse and then use foreign tax credit on US return.

lina.payroll: Opening vendor ticket now. payroll-bot: case_id=DUP-MX-4120. Assigned: lina.payroll. Vendor ETA: 24h initial response.

isabel.legal: FYI if the PEO submitted payroll taxes, there could be employer-side liabilities in MX (IMSS, ISR). We need indemnity language from vendor and to confirm we did not authorize local employment. Also collect any signed paperwork that mistakenly set you as local employee.

lina.payroll: Vendor responded: they confirmed an erroneous EOR flag on Diego9s profile triggered a one-off run. They say bank recall is possible if initiated within 2 business days. They are checking whether CFDI was generated and whether taxes were remitted.

carlos.tax: Two tax scenarios to prepare:
- Best case: no CFDI generated, vendor recalls payment, no MX reporting -> simple reversal.
- If CFDI generated but taxes not remitted: cancel CFDI and reverse net pay, employer must correct employer filings.
- Worst case: CFDI generated and taxes remitted -> funds will need to be repaid by company, and Diego may need documentation to claim foreign tax credit if Mexican taxes are withheld ultimately.

diego.mendez: Please try to recall. The MX deposit already cleared into my account though. Bank shows credited today at 10:04 MXT.

lina.payroll: Noted. I'll request immediate recall and ask vendor to start CFDI cancellation if necessary. Please DO NOT spend the MXN funds until we confirm. We'll either reverse or instruct you on the reimbursement flow.

isabel.legal: I'll request vendor indemnity that any employer liabilities arising from this error are the vendor's responsibility. Also preparing a short employee letter explaining the error for your tax records.

payroll-bot: Vendor confirmed recall request submitted. ticket=DUP-MX-4120. Vendor says recall success probability: high if taxes not remitted. Next update in 24h.

lina.payroll: Quick heads-up: if we must reimburse MX taxes, payroll policy requires company to cover employer taxes; employee may be made whole for net pay. We'll coordinate gross-up or repayment depending on tax counsel advice.

carlos.tax: If MX taxes are ultimately remitted and cannot be reversed, we'll provide Diego with documentation of Mexican tax withheld so he can claim foreign tax credit on his US Form 1116. We'll also assess whether treaty/totalization relief applies (likely not for employment taxes).

diego.mendez: Thanks. Appreciate the quick response. Let me know if you need any more docs.

lina.payroll: Got it. Please keep the portal docs and don't move the MX funds. I'll update the case when vendor confirms recall or CFDI cancellation. ETA 24h.

payroll-bot: Case DUP-MX-4120 updated. Reminder: employee to keep screenshots of bank entries and not spend MXN deposit.
